title: Three Days and One Short Ticket
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：speed　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 speed 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the driver ① kept the speed that no passenger in the station would have noted, and he said the keeping was the whole of the day. The ② speed, meaning the rate itself and not the ticket, ran three days and stayed unnoted in the book; speed, he said, is the only thing in a station that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ sort of speed in that station had the same short ticket beside it, and the ④ speed at the far platform, meaning the seat they kept for the children to book and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Speed, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the driver said the noting is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the speed was the whole of the matter, meaning the rush and not the rate. The ⑥ speed, meaning the rush and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; speed, he said, is either something you keep or the only word that means both rate and a rush. He said the rush is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ speed had become a line in a timetable, and the timetable had become an argument about the short ticket. The ⑧ speed of the whole thing, the driver wrote in February, was one station and three days of noting; speed, he said, is either the seat at the far platform or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ speed I remember is the speed noted in the timetable, which closed in 1962 and is still noted as the quietest in the station. ⑩ Speed, my mother said in 1964, is the only thing that improves by being noted; all speed, she said, is a rush that has agreed to look like rate. She said the rush was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 速度（指车站里每一类旁边的那一类）
B. n. 速度（指那种速度本身，与薄薄的车票相对）
C. 固定搭配：keep the speed 保持这一种速度
D. n. 速度（指留给孩子们订的那一个）
E. n. 速度之事（抽象总称，指一处车站的速度之事）
F. n. 速度（指时刻表里写到、被记下的那一种）
G. n. 速度、急切（指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 急切（抽象总称，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: kept the speed that no passenger in the station would have noted
The speed, meaning the rate itself and not the ticket
Every sort of speed in that station
the speed at the far platform
the speed was the whole of the matter
the speed had become a line in a timetable
The speed of the whole thing

answers.why: keep the speed 意为“保持这一种速度”，1955 年那位司机把车站里没有一位乘客肯记下的一种速度做了一遍。
speed 意为“速度”，指那种速度本身而不是薄薄的车票，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被记下。
speed 意为“速度”，指车站里每一类旁边的那一类，每一类旁边都有同一张薄薄的车票。
speed 意为“速度”，指最远那座站台的留给孩子们订的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
speed 意为“速度、急切”，指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这种急切就是那件事的全部。
speed 意为“急切”，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西而不是那种速度，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
speed 意为“速度”，指时刻表里写到、被记下的那一种，到 1960 年这一种成了时刻表里的一行。
speed 意为“速度之事”，司机二月写道，整件事的速度之事是一处车站和三个日子的记下。
speed 意为“速度”，我记得的是时刻表里记下过的那一种，1962 年到站了，至今仍被说成车站里最安静的一种。
speed 为抽象总称，母亲 1964 年说，速度是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的速度。
